title: Let an agent add and schedule listings on your directory site
summary: Piotr Kulpinski connected Claude Code to his directory app; he reports it added, filled in and scheduled a listing in 7 steps and 54 seconds.
agent_role: Claude Code checked for duplicates, read categories, created a draft, filled it from the website and scheduled it. The human gave one sentence and built the safety rules.
outcome: Author reports 7 tool calls in 54 seconds, with only a screenshot missing because local storage wasn't set up.
what_they_did: The developer exposed his directory app's existing admin actions to AI agents through a connector. He kept a read-only public side and a password-protected admin side. He gave Claude Code one sentence asking it to add a site. There is no delete action and new entries start as drafts.
how_it_went: He says the agent checked for duplicates, picked categories and tags, filled the description and icon, and scheduled the listing in 54 seconds. Earlier runs were less clean.
worth_knowing: Treat user-written text as data, not instructions, and turn off owner emails by default so bulk agent edits don't spam people.
prompt: Using my directory site's admin connector, add [website URL] as a new listing. First check it isn't already listed. Read the available categories and tags, create a draft, and fill in the description from the website. Show me the draft and wait for approval before scheduling it for the next free publish day.

curation.rationale: A real agent session with concrete numbers and code, though it promotes the author's paid product.
